passages.source_text: ἡ δὲ ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ὁρισθεῖσα θρησκεία ἐστὶν αὕτη Τὸ μόνον αὐτὸν σέβειν καὶ τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας μόνῳ πιστεύειν προφήτῃ καὶ „εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν“ βαπτισθῆναι καὶ οὕτως διὰ τῆς ἁγνοτάτης βαφῆς ἀναγεννηθῆναι θεῷ διὰ τοῦ σώζοντος ὕδατος, „τραπέζης δαιμόνων“ μὴ μεταλαμβάνειν (λέγω δὲ εἰδωλοθύτων, νεκρῶν, πνικτῶν, θηριαλώτων, αἵματος), μὴ ἀκαθάρτως βιοῦν, ἀπὸ κοίτης γυναικὸς λούεσθαι, αὐτὰς μέντοι καὶ ἄφεδρον φυλάσσειν, πάντας δὲ σωφρονεῖν, εὖ ποιεῖν, μὴ ἀδικεῖν, παρὰ τοῦ πάντα δυναμένου θεοῦ ζωὴν αἰώνιον προσδοκᾶν, εὐχαῖς καὶ δεήσεσιν συνεχέσιν αἰτουμένους αὐτὴν λαβεῖν. τοιαῦτα καὶ ἐν τῇ Σιδῶνι τοῦ Πέτρου παραινοῦντος, ἡμέραις ὀλίγαις πολλῶν κἀκεῖ μετανοησάντων καὶ πιστευσάντων καὶ θεραπευθέντων ἐκκλησίαν συνέστησεν καὶ τῶν συνεπομένων αὐτῷ πρεσβυτέρων τινὰ καταστήσας αὐτοῖς ἐπίσκοπον ἐξῄει τῆς Σιδῶνος.

Τάδε δοκεῖ τῷ παντεπόπτῃ θεῷ, μηδενὸς ἀνθρώπων ὑμᾶς κυριεύειν μηδὲ παρενοχλεῖν μηδενί, ἐὰν μή τις ἑαυτὸν ὑμῖν καταδουλώσῃ, προσκυνῶν ὑμᾶς καὶ θύων καὶ σπένδων καὶ τῆς ὑμετέρας μεταλαμβάνων τραπέζης ἢ ἕτερόν τι ὧν οὐ χρὴ ἐκτελῶν ἢ αἷμα χέων ἢ σαρκῶν νεκρῶν γευόμενος ἢ θηρίου λειψάνου ἢ τμητοῦ ἢ πνικτοῦ ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς ἀκαθάρτου ἐμπιπλάμενος. τῶν δὲ νόμῳ ἐμῷ προσφευγόντων οὐ μόνον οὐ ψαύσετε, ἀλλὰ καὶ τιμὴν δώσετε, καὶ ἐκ προσώπου φεύξεσθε. ὅ,τι γὰρ ἂν αὐτοῖς δικαίοις οὖσι καθ’ ὑμῶν δοκῇ, τοῦθ’ ὑμᾶς δεήσει παθεῖν. ἐὰν δὲ τινὲς τῶν ἐμοὶ προσκειμένων ἐξαμάρτωσιν, ἢ· μοιχευσάμενοι ἢ μαγεύσαντες ἢ ἀκαθάρτως βιώσαντες ἢ ἄλλο τι τῶν ἐμοὶ μὴ δοκούντων πράξαντες, τότε-ἐξ ἐμῆς κελεύσεως πάσχειν τι αὐτοὺς ὑφ’ ὑμῶν ἢ ὑφ’ ἑτέρων δεήσει· οἷς καὶ μετανοήσασιν, τὴν μετάνοιαν κρίνας εἴτε ἀξία ἐστὶν συγγνώμης εἴτε καὶ οὔ, τὴν ἀπόφασιν ποιήσομαι. ταῦτα οὖν μνημονεύειν καὶ ποιεῖν ὀφείλετε, εὖ εἰδότες ὅτι οὐδὲ αἱ ἐνθυμήσεις ὑμῶν λαθεῖν αὐτὸν δυνήσονται.

ἀλλ᾽. ὅμως κἂν πάντες δαίμονες μετὰ πάντων τῶν παθῶν ὑμᾶς φεύγωσιν, οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν τούτῳ μόνον χαίρειν, ἀλλ᾽ ἐν τῷ δι᾽ εὐαρεστίαν τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ἐν οὐρανῷ ὡς ἀεὶ ζώντων ἀναγραφῆναι. οὕτω καὶ τὸ θεῖον ἅγιον πνεῦμα χαίρει ὅτι τὸν θάνατον νενίκηκεν ἄνθρωπος· τὸ γὰρ δαίμονας φυγαδεύειν εἰς τὴν ἄλλου ἴασιν γίνεται. ταῦτα δὲ λέγομεν οὐχ ὡς ἀρνούμενοι τὸ μὴ δεῖν ἄλλοις βοηθεῖν, ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι μὴ χρὴ ἐπὶ τούτῳ τυφωθέντας ἑαυτῶν ἀμελεῖν. ἔσθ’ ὅτε δέ τινας ἀνόμους ἄνδρας δαίμονες φεύγουσιν δι’ ὄνομα τίμιον καὶ ἐνεδρεύονται ὅ τε ἀπελάσας καὶ ὁ ἱστορήσας· ὁ μὲν ἀπελάσας ὡς διὰ δικαιοσύνην προτιμηθεὶς οὐκ εἰδὼς τοῦ δαίμονος τὸ κακοῦργον (ἅμα τε γὰρ τὸ ὄνομα τετίμηκεν καὶ τῇ φυγῇ τὸν ἀσεβῆ εἰς οἴησιν δικαιοσύνης περιβαλὼν τοῦ μὴ μετανοεῖν ἠπάτησεν), ὁ δὲ ἱστορήσας ὡς εὐσεβεῖ συγχρησάμενος τῷ ἀπελάσαντι πρὸς τὴν ὁμοίαν πολιτείαν σπεύσας ἀπόλλυται. ἐνίοτε δὲ καὶ τοὺς μὴ θεῷ προσκειμένους ὅρκους φεύγειν ὑποκρίνονται, ἵν’ ἀπατήσαντες αὐτοὺς ὅτε θελήσωσιν ἀνέλωσιν.

ὅτι δὲ ὄντως ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ταῖς τῶν πεπλανημένων εὐποιίαις αἱ τῶν ἀλήθειαν ἐγνωκότων ἰσάζονται πράξεις, αὐτὸς ἡμᾶς ὁ ἀψευδὴς ἐδίδαξεν...., εἰπὼν πρὸς μὲν τοὺς ἀμελοῦντας ἐλθεῖν καὶ ἐπακούειν αὐτοῦ „βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται μετὰ .τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτήν, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἀπὸ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος· καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε, καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε“. πρὸς δὲ τοὺς ἐν τῷ λαῷ μὴ θέλοντας μετανοῆσαι ἐπὶ τῷ κηρύγματι αὐτοῦ εἶπεν „ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἐγερθήσονται μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν, ὅτι ἀκούσαντες μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ· καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον ... ὧδε, καὶ οὐδεὶς πιστεύει“. καὶ οὕτως πρὸς πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν αὐτῶν ἀντιπαραθεὶς τοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν πεποιηκότας εἰς κατάκρισιν τῶν ἐν θεοσεβείᾳ μηδὲ τὸ ἴσον καλὸν τοῖς πεπλανημένοις πεποιηκότων, τοὺς ἔχοντας λογισμὸν ἐνουθέτει μὴ μόνον ὅσα τοῖς ἔθνεσιν τὰ καλὰ ἴσως ποιεῖν, ἀλλὰ τὸ πλεῖον. ὁ δὲ λόγος μοι ἐρρύη, πρόφασιν λαβὼν ἐκ τοῦ δεῖν φυλάσσειν τὴν ἄφεδρον καὶ ἀπὸ κοινωνίας βαπτίζεσθαι, μὴ ἀρνεῖσθαι τὴν τοιαύτην ἁγνείαν, κἂν οἱ πεπλανημένοι αὐτὴν πράττωσιν, ὅτε εἰς κατάκρισιν τῶν ἐν θεοσεβείᾳ εἰσὶν οἱ ἐν πλάνῃ ποιοῦντες καλῶς μετὰ τοῦ μὴ σῴζεσθαι· ὅτι ἡ τιμὴ τῆς ἁγνείας αὐτῶν ἐστὶ διὰ τὴν πλάνην καὶ οὐ διὰ θρησκείαν τοῦ ὄντως πατρὸς καὶ θεοῦ τῶν ὅλων.

κἀγὼ πρὸς ταῦτα ἀπεκρινάμην Οὐκοῦν οἱ ἀδικοῦντες οὐκ εἰσὶν αἴτιοι, ὅτι κρίσει θεοῦ ἀδικοῦσιν τοὺς δικαίους. καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἔφη Καὶ πάνυ ἁμαρτάνουσιν, πρὸς γὰρ τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν ἑαυτοὺς ἀποδεδωκότες. ὅθεν εἰδὼς ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν ἐκλέγεται τιμωρεῖν τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῖς προτέροις ἁμαρτήμασιν μεταμεληθέντας δικαίως, ἵνα τοῖς μὲν δικαίοις διὰ τῆς τοιαύτης τιμωρίας τὰ πρὸ τῆς μετανοίας πραχθέντα ἀφεθῇ κακά, τοῖς δὲ τιμωροῦσιν ἀσεβέσιν κακουχεῖν ἐπιθυμοῦσιν καὶ μετανοεῖν μὴ θέλουσιν εἰς ἀναπλήρωσιν ἰδίας κολάσεως δικαίους κακουχεῖν συνεχωρήθη· ἄνευ γὰρ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ βουλῆς οὐδὲ στρουθὸς ἐν παγίδι ἐνπεσεῖν ἔχει· οὕτως δικαίων καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῷ θεῷ ἐναρίθμιοί εἰσιν.

ἰδὲ οἵῳ θεῷ, Σίμων, ἀχαριστεῖν ἡμᾶς πεῖσαι θέλεις· καὶ βαστάζει σε ἡ γῆ, ἴσως δὲ ἰδεῖν βουλομένῃ τίς σοι τὰ ὅμοια φρονεῖν τολμήσοι. πρῶτος γὰρ ἐτόλμησας, ὃ μηδεὶς ἐτόλμησεν· πρῶτος ἐφθέγξω, ἃ πρώτως ἠκούσαμεν. πρῶτοι καὶ μόνοι ἡμεῖς ἐπὶ τοιαύτῃ σου ἀσεβείᾳ τὴν ἄπειρον τοῦ θεοῦ μακροθυμίαν ἱστορήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἄλλου τινὸς ἢ τοῦ κτίσαντος τὸν κόσμον, εἰς ὃν ἀσεβεῖν ἐτόλμησας. καὶ χάσματα γῆς οὐκ ἐγενήθη καὶ πῦρ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ οὐ κατεπέμφθη καὶ εἰς ἐμπρησμὸν ἀνδρῶν οὐκ ἐπεξῆλθεν, καὶ ὑετὸς οὐκ ἐπεσχέθη καὶ θηρῶν πλῆθος ἀπὸ δρυμῶν οὐκ ἐπέμφθη, καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἡμᾶς διὰ ἕνα ἁμαρτάνοντα ὡς ἐπὶ μοιχείας πνευματικῆς τῆς κατὰ σάρκα χείρονος ὑπαρχούσης ἡ θεοῦ ὀργὴ ὀλέθριος οὐκ ἤρξατο. οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ὁ τότε ἐπεξελθὼν τὰ ἁμαρτήματα οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς κτίστης θεός; ἐπεὶ καὶ νῦν τὰ μέγιστα βλασφημούμενος τὰ μέγιστα ἐπεξήρχετο. ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον μακροθυμεῖ, εἰς μετάνοιαν καλεῖ, συντελοῦντα βέλη πρὸς συντέλειαν τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἐν τοῖς θησαυροῖς ἀποκείμενα ἔχων, ἅτινα ἐπαφήσει ὡς ζῷα ἔμψυχα, ὅταν ἀνταποδοῦναι κρίσιν τοῖς ἐχθροῖς αὐτοῦ προκαθεσθῇ. διὸ φοβηθῶμεν θεὸν δίκαιον, οὗ τὴν μορφὴν πρὸς τιμὴν τὸ ἀνθρώπου βαστάζει σῶμα.

translation_policy_text:
# Translation Stance

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Contested terms

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Greek / Hebrew | Default English | Alternatives considered | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |
| δοῦλος *doulos* | servant | bondservant, slave | Uses reader-facing "servant" consistently; documents bonded-status and ownership nuance in notes/audit metadata |
| πίστις *pistis* | faith | faithfulness, trust | Main text: faith; footnote alternatives where contested |
| δικαιοσύνη *dikaiosynē* | righteousness | justice | Both renderings preserved in footnotes for Pauline passages |
| ἱλαστήριον *hilastērion* | atoning sacrifice | propitiation, mercy seat | Dynamic rendering for accessibility; alternatives footnoted |
| ἀγάπη *agapē* | love | charity (archaic) | Lexical cognates in source kept |
| σάρξ *sarx* | flesh (literal) / sinful nature (metaphorical) | — | Context-dependent; per-verse documented |
| μετανοέω / μετάνοια *metanoeō / metanoia* | repent / repentance where context supports moral-spiritual change | change of mind, reconsider, regret and other contextual renderings | See "Repentance terminology (2026-10-13)"; explain the meaning without homogenizing distinct source expressions |
| νήφω *nēphō* | clear-minded (most contexts); sober (where Paul explicitly runs the drunk/sober metaphor) | sober-minded | See revision notes in 1 Pet 5:8, 1 Thess 5:6 |
| יְהוָה YHWH | Yahweh | the LORD, Jehovah | Renders the divine name as a name. Where the NT quotes an OT YHWH passage using *Kyrios*, the NT verse retains "Lord" to preserve the Greek; the OT source verse uses "Yahweh". |
| אָדָם *adam* | man / humankind (context) | — | Context-dependent per usage |

## Repentance terminology (2026-10-13)

The contextual reassessment supersedes the October 11 reorientation default.
Use **repent / repentance** for the moral-spiritual response where the passage
supports it. Familiarity alone is not evidence of accuracy; explain the intended
change of disposition and conduct rather than reducing repentance to sadness
or a change of opinion. Reorientation can explain the concept but is not a
mandatory replacement in reader text. No claim about measured reader reception
or independent scholarly approval is made.

**Context still controls.** Retain regret, remorse, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where those fit the source and local direction.
Preserve contested readings in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17, the alternate turning
reading in Jeremiah 31:19, and distinct turn/return verbs in Acts 3:19 and 26:20.
Use "repentance toward God" in Acts 20:21 because the sentence explicitly gives
that direction; do not insert it into every occurrence of metanoia.

Keep sorrow and repentance distinct in 2 Corinthians 7:9-10. Retain the
relationship between repentance and its fruits, rather than equating the two.
Use "I repent" in Luke 17:4 without requiring proof of completed reform before
forgiveness. Preserve baptismal grammar without deciding symbolic versus causal
interpretations by a vocabulary substitution.

Do not add intensifiers. Keep source-backed emphasis such as the existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" in Hermas 21:4. Keep the corrected
"more joy ... than" in Luke 15:7. Extra-canonical writers retain their own
conceptual frameworks, including adverse changes of mind; do not harmonize
them to a canonical Godward formula. Historical English witnesses and source
transcriptions remain untouched; reader adaptations retain their disclosure.

All **397** previously changed records have an explicit new decision, including
retained exceptions and the four October 12 follow-up records. Earlier wording,
notes, plans, and review history are preserved rather than erased. See the
[full decision ledger](docs/REPENTANCE_REASSESSMENT_2026-10-13.md) and exact,
hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/repentance-contextual-2026-10-13.json`.
These remain editorial drafts, not independent scholarly certifications.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

## Change log for this document

Material changes to this document are themselves commits. Prior
versions of the stance are preserved in git history.

- **2026-04-21:** Removed creedal affirmations (Apostles' Creed,
  Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition) and replaced with a
  theological-stance section that declines specific creedal
  commitment. Translation philosophy and contested-terms table
  preserved unchanged; those are methodology, not creedal
  commitment, and the project actually runs on them. Added a
  "Translating into other languages" section stating POB's long-
  term intention to ship in every feasible major language, with
  the full revision pipeline and transparent supported-language
  disclosure. Per-verse YAML citing the old `doctrine_reference`
  values is preserved as historical record; those are not
  retroactively edited.
ambiguity_standard: Apply the supplied DOCTRINE.md ambiguity policy: a defensible contextual rendering may be used in the main text when material alternatives and the reason for the choice are preserved in notes. A unique or uncontested interpretation is not required. Distinguish (a) an unreadable or unverified source, omitted content, invented restoration, or a construction for which no defensible English can be given, from (b) ordinary lexical, attachment, or referent ambiguity faithfully preserved in English or explained with viable alternatives. The former blocks publication; the latter does not automatically block it. A note cannot excuse unsupported wording: the proposed main rendering must itself be defensible from the supplied Greek. Clearly printed gaps must remain gaps, not be filled by invention. Never change a verdict merely to achieve acceptance.
selected_edition_coverage_standard: Coverage is assessed against ALL SURVIVING WORDING AND PRINTED GAP MARKERS in the selected image-checked edition, not against unavailable words of a hypothetical complete original. A confirmed printed lacuna must remain an explicit gap in the English, retaining the exact number of printed dots (layout whitespace may differ), with a source-quoted note explaining that its content is unavailable and no restoration has been supplied. Such faithful representation can pass selected-edition coverage; it must never be described as recovery of the lost wording or an unbroken original. Distinguish this from missing scan pages, unverified ink, omitted surviving Greek, an unsupported English completion, or a translation that obscures the gap: those remain blocking. Neither this scope clarification nor a prior suggestion is an instruction to accept a draft; independently check every surviving clause, every gap, and every disclosure.
authorization: Human approved Codex translators and independently checked public-domain Greek source corrections; originals must be preserved in notes and fresh independent Sol6.1 review is mandatory
curation_pin_status: New source curations pending Git pin; final export must bind their actual canonical commit

previous_passages.text: The religious observance appointed by him is this: to worship him alone; to believe the one prophet of truth; to be baptized “for forgiveness of sins” and thus, through the purest immersion, to be born anew to God through the water that saves; not to partake of “a table of demons” (I mean things sacrificed to idols, animals found dead, strangled animals, animals caught by wild beasts, and blood); not to live in impurity; to bathe after intercourse with a woman, while women themselves must also observe menstrual separation; for everyone to practice self-control, do good, and not act unjustly; and to await eternal life from the all-powerful God, asking through continual prayers and petitions to receive it. As Peter gave such exhortations also in Sidon, within a few days many there too reoriented themselves, believed, and were healed. He established a church, appointed one of the elders accompanying him as their overseer, and departed from Sidon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας μόνῳ πιστεύειν προφήτῃ
lexical_decisions.chosen: to believe the one prophet of truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: μόνῳ characterizes the prophet as the sole or one prophet of truth. The phrase could also be rendered “to believe only the prophet of truth,” with the exclusivity attached adverbially to believing.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through the purest immersion
lexical_decisions.rationale: βαφή denotes dipping or immersion and here refers to the preceding baptism; the superlative force of ἁγνοτάτης is retained.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀναγεννηθῆναι θεῷ διὰ τοῦ σώζοντος ὕδατος
lexical_decisions.chosen: to be born anew to God through the water that saves
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves both the God-directed dative θεῷ and the source’s direct description of the water as saving.

lexical_decisions.chosen: animals found dead, strangled animals, animals caught by wild beasts
lexical_decisions.rationale: These substantivized plurals occur in a list of prohibited foods. “Animals found dead” expresses νεκρῶν contextually; more literally it is simply “dead things.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: to bathe after intercourse with a woman
lexical_decisions.rationale: κοίτη γυναικός literally refers to a woman’s bed but in this purity context denotes sexual intercourse.

lexical_decisions.chosen: while women themselves must also observe menstrual separation
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἄφεδρος is a term for menstruation or the associated period of separation. The phrase may also be rendered “observe the menstrual period”; the source does not explicitly repeat the preceding command to bathe.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοιαῦτα καὶ ἐν τῇ Σιδῶνι τοῦ Πέτρου παραινοῦντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: As Peter gave such exhortations also in Sidon
lexical_decisions.rationale: The additive καί is preserved with “also,” explicitly stating that Peter gave such exhortations in Sidon as well. This is distinct from the later κἀκεῖ, rendered “there too,” which characterizes the people’s response.

lexical_decisions.chosen: reoriented themselves
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context describes moral and religious redirection accompanying belief; the traditional alternative is “repented.” No Godward phrase is added because the Greek does not state one here.

lexical_decisions.chosen: overseer
lexical_decisions.rationale: The word designates the supervisory office assigned to the elder; “bishop” is a possible institutional rendering but may imply a later fixed title.

previous_passages.text: “This is the will of the all-seeing God: you are to rule over no human being and trouble no one, unless someone enslaves himself to you by worshiping you and sacrificing and pouring libations and sharing in your table, or by doing anything else that ought not to be done, or by shedding blood, or by tasting dead flesh, or by filling himself with the remains of a wild animal, or with something cut up, or with something strangled, or with any other impure thing. Those who take refuge in my law you will not even touch; instead, you will give them honor and flee from their presence. For whatever they, being righteous, decide against you, you will have to suffer. But if any of those devoted to me sin, whether by committing adultery, practicing magic, living impurely, or doing anything else that does not meet with my approval, then, at my command, they will have to suffer something at your hands or at the hands of others. And if they reorient, I will judge their reorientation, whether it is worthy of forgiveness or not, and make my decision. So you must remember and do these things, knowing well that not even your thoughts will be able to escape his notice.”

source_issues.issue: The genitive can refer to remains belonging to a wild animal or remains left by one. The main rendering retains the first defensible reading; the alternative is remains left by a wild animal, that is, its leavings. No lost wording is assumed.

The precise dietary category is not specified by this standalone substantivized adjective. Cut up preserves its cutting sense; mutilated is another possible rendering. It has not been expanded into a particular animal part or a specified method of slaughter.

lexical_decisions.chosen: This is the will of the all-seeing God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The decree formula literally states what seems good to God; will conveys its prescriptive force in this setting. παντεπόπτῃ is all-seeing.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐὰν μή τις ἑαυτὸν ὑμῖν καταδουλώσῃ
lexical_decisions.chosen: unless someone enslaves himself to you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb describes placing oneself under another’s ownership or domination, not merely voluntary service. The POB main-text servant convention concerns the noun δοῦλος; here enslaves preserves the explicit verbal subjugation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: or by tasting dead flesh
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both flesh and dead without making the phrase exclusively human flesh. Flesh of the dead is a viable alternative if νεκρῶν is taken substantivally; the source here does not specify the species.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἢ θηρίου λειψάνου ἢ τμητοῦ ἢ πνικτοῦ ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς ἀκαθάρτου ἐμπιπλάμενος.
lexical_decisions.chosen: or by filling himself with the remains of a wild animal, or with something cut up, or with something strangled, or with any other impure thing.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains all items and the filling/eating construction. θηρίου λειψάνου can describe a wild animal’s remains or remains left by a wild animal; the main text preserves the former grammatical reading. τμητοῦ literally denotes something cut, cut up, or mutilated; no specific unprinted slaughter rule is imposed. πνικτοῦ denotes something strangled or choked.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν δὲ νόμῳ ἐμῷ προσφευγόντων οὐ μόνον οὐ ψαύσετε, ἀλλὰ καὶ τιμὴν δώσετε, καὶ ἐκ προσώπου φεύξεσθε.
lexical_decisions.chosen: Those who take refuge in my law you will not even touch; instead, you will give them honor and flee from their presence.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the refuge metaphor, the prohibition on touching, the additional requirement of honor, and flight from their presence. My is retained as the divine first-person speech, rather than normalizing the whole speech to third person.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅ,τι γὰρ ἂν αὐτοῖς δικαίοις οὖσι καθ’ ὑμῶν δοκῇ, τοῦθ’ ὑμᾶς δεήσει παθεῖν.
lexical_decisions.chosen: For whatever they, being righteous, decide against you, you will have to suffer.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Represents the open-ended decision against the demons and its compulsory consequence, with being righteous retained rather than expanded into an unprinted condition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἷς καὶ μετανοήσασιν, τὴν μετάνοιαν κρίνας εἴτε ἀξία ἐστὶν συγγνώμης εἴτε καὶ οὔ, τὴν ἀπόφασιν ποιήσομαι.
lexical_decisions.chosen: And if they reorient, I will judge their reorientation, whether it is worthy of forgiveness or not, and make my decision.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses POB reorient/reorientation for moral-spiritual redirection, traditionally repent/repentance, without inventing an intensifier or adding a destination. The divine judgment, possibility of forgiveness, and possibility of non-forgiveness are all retained. The participial construction is expressed as an English conditional.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εὖ εἰδότες ὅτι οὐδὲ αἱ ἐνθυμήσεις ὑμῶν λαθεῖν αὐτὸν δυνήσονται.
lexical_decisions.chosen: knowing well that not even your thoughts will be able to escape his notice.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the Greek’s return to third-person him at the end of speech otherwise containing divine first-person language; it is not silently harmonized to my notice.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: προσκυνῶν ὑμᾶς καὶ θύων καὶ σπένδων καὶ τῆς ὑμετέρας μεταλαμβάνων τραπέζης ἢ ἕτερόν τι ὧν οὐ χρὴ ἐκτελῶν ἢ αἷμα χέων ἢ σαρκῶν νεκρῶν γευόμενος
lexical_decisions.chosen: by worshiping you and sacrificing and pouring libations and sharing in your table, or by doing anything else that ought not to be done, or by shedding blood, or by tasting dead flesh
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated and preserves the initial καί-linked ritual sequence, while the repeated or retains the subsequent ἤ-linked alternatives. This rendering represents the coordination without adding a claim that all initial acts must be performed jointly as a necessary condition of subjugation.

previous_passages.text: But nevertheless, even if all demons together with all afflictions flee from you, you must not rejoice in this alone, but in the fact that, because you have proved pleasing, your names have been inscribed in heaven as those of people who live forever. Thus the divine Holy Spirit too rejoices because a human being has conquered death; for the expulsion of demons takes place for someone else’s healing. We say these things, however, not as people who deny the claim that there is no need to help others, but because one must not grow conceited over this and neglect oneself. Sometimes demons flee some lawless men because of an honored name, and both the one who drove them away and the one who witnessed what happened are ambushed. The one who drove them away is ambushed as though he had been favored because of righteousness, not knowing the demon’s villainy (for the demon has both honored the name and, by its flight, wrapped the impious man in a conceit of righteousness and deceived him into not reorienting); but the one who witnessed what happened, having associated with the one who drove them away as with a devout man and having hastened toward the same way of life, perishes. At times they also pretend to flee oaths not connected with God, so that, after deceiving them, they may destroy them whenever they wish.

source_issues.issue: The printed period separates the elided conjunction ἀλλ᾽ from ὅμως, leaving ἀλλ᾽ abruptly isolated. The translation reads the two together as “But nevertheless” while retaining both words.

source_issues.source_quote: οὐχ ὡς ἀρνούμενοι τὸ μὴ δεῖν ἄλλοις βοηθεῖν
source_issues.issue: As printed, the nested negatives mean “not as denying the claim that there is no need to help others,” and that sense is retained in the translation. It is contextually awkward because the following clause warns only against neglecting oneself, and an intrusive μή may be suspected. The surviving wording nevertheless permits a defensible literal translation.
source_issues.proposed_reading: οὐχ ὡς ἀρνούμενοι τὸ δεῖν ἄλλοις βοηθεῖν

lexical_decisions.chosen: because you have proved pleasing
lexical_decisions.rationale: εὐαρεστία denotes being pleasing or acceptable. God is the likely implied evaluator, but the Greek does not state the referent explicitly.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the divine Holy Spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: The article and paired adjectives present the spirit as the divine holy spirit in view; capitalization reflects the personal theological referent without adding a title absent from the wording.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who witnessed what happened
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἱστορέω can mean to observe, investigate, inquire about, visit, or recount. Here it denotes the person who learns of or observes the expulsion and consequently treats the exorcist as devout.

lexical_decisions.chosen: wrapped the impious man in a conceit of righteousness
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the clothing or enveloping image of περιβάλλω; οἴησις may mean an opinion, supposition, or conceited belief.

lexical_decisions.chosen: deceived him into not reorienting
lexical_decisions.rationale: The articular infinitive expresses the outcome sought by the deception. “Reorienting” follows the supplied terminology policy; “repenting” is the traditional alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: oaths not connected with God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle grammatically modifies ὅρκους and describes oaths not attached or devoted to God. Context may imply “oaths used by people not devoted to God,” but those people are not explicitly named in this phrase.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵν’ ἀπατήσαντες αὐτοὺς ὅτε θελήσωσιν ἀνέλωσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that, after deceiving them, they may destroy them whenever they wish
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated masculine pronoun is preserved without supplying an explicit antecedent. It most plausibly concerns the people relying on the oaths, though grammatically it can refer back to the masculine plural ὅρκους.

previous_passages.text: That on the day of judgment the actions of those who have known the truth are indeed placed on an equal footing with the good deeds of those who have been deceived, the one who does not lie himself taught us ...., saying to those who neglected to come and listen to him, “The queen of the south will rise with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and look, something greater than Solomon is here, and you do not believe.” To those among the people who were unwilling to reorient at his proclamation, he said, “Men of Nineveh will rise with this generation and condemn it, because on hearing they reoriented in response to Jonah’s proclamation; and look, something greater ... is here, and no one believes.” Thus, setting over against each of their acts of impiety those from the nations who had acted, to condemn those in reverence toward God who had not done even as much good as those who had been deceived, he admonished those with understanding not merely to do good things equally with the nations, but to do more. My discourse flowed on, taking its starting point from the need to observe menstrual separation and to immerse oneself after intercourse: not to reject such purity even if those who have been deceived practice it, since those in error who do good serve to condemn those in reverence toward God, although they themselves are not saved. For their honoring of purity is because of error, not because of worship of the true Father and God of all.

source_issues.issue: Exactly 4 printed gap dots remain in the English; no unavailable words are restored.
Exactly 3 printed gap dots remain in the English; no unavailable words are restored.

The selected edition supplies an isolated dot before τῆς. English reads the phrase with this generation across that punctuation. This single dot is distinguished from the section’s four-dot and three-dot printed gaps; it is not called an OCR error and no replacement Greek is proposed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who does not lie himself taught us ....
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected edition has four gap dots; exactly four remain, without reconstruction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and look, something greater ... is here
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly three gap dots remain. No familiar proper name from another witness is supplied.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they reoriented in response to Jonah’s proclamation
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses POB reorientation terminology, traditionally repented, preserving the stated occasion of the response.

lexical_decisions.chosen: although they themselves are not saved
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the author’s explicit non-salvation claim about people in error who nonetheless do good.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to observe menstrual separation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The purity context concerns observance of menstrual separation, not merely monitoring a cycle. The menstrual period is a viable temporal rendering; if the noun is taken personally, the menstruating woman is another possible referent. The main text selects the separation observance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: their honoring of purity
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context of people practicing purity supports τιμή as their valuing or honoring the practice, with αὐτῶν related to that honoring. The esteem or value of their purity, attaching αὐτῶν to ἁγνείας, is a material alternative and is not excluded by the main rendering.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ταῖς τῶν πεπλανημένων εὐποιίαις αἱ τῶν ἀλήθειαν ἐγνωκότων ἰσάζονται πράξεις
lexical_decisions.chosen: the actions of those who have known the truth are indeed placed on an equal footing with the good deeds of those who have been deceived
lexical_decisions.rationale: Placed on an equal footing preserves the equality force of ἰσάζονται, central to the subsequent equal-good versus doing-more argument. It does not decide that every particular action necessarily receives an identical valuation; measured against alone would state comparison without the explicit equal-footing force.

previous_passages.text: And in response I said, “Then those who do wrong are not responsible, since it is by God’s judgment that they wrong the righteous.” Peter said, “They most certainly do sin, for they have given themselves over to sinning. Therefore, with this knowledge, he chooses some from among them to punish justly those who have come to regret their former sins, so that, for the righteous, through punishment of this kind, the evil deeds done before their reorientation may be forgiven, while the ungodly punishers, who desire to maltreat others and are unwilling to reorient, have been permitted to maltreat the righteous in order to fill up the measure of their own penalty. For without God’s counsel not even a sparrow can fall into a trap; in the same way, even the hairs of the righteous are numbered by God.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅθεν εἰδὼς ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν ἐκλέγεται τιμωρεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Therefore, with this knowledge, he chooses some from among them to punish
lexical_decisions.rationale: The subject is understood contextually as God, while the people chosen from among the wrongdoers are the understood subjects of the infinitive “to punish.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῖς προτέροις ἁμαρτήμασιν μεταμεληθέντας δικαίως
lexical_decisions.chosen: those who have come to regret their former sins ... justly
lexical_decisions.rationale: μεταμέλομαι is distinguished from the subsequent μετάνοια language and rendered as regret. δικαίως is attached to the justice of the punishment; it could instead describe their regretting as rightly done.

lexical_decisions.chosen: before their reorientation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering follows the supplied terminology policy for μετάνοια while not adding an unstated destination such as “toward God.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: are unwilling to reorient
lexical_decisions.rationale: The moral redirection sense of μετανοεῖν is retained without an invented intensifier or destination.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in order to fill up the measure of their own penalty
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀναπλήρωσις denotes filling up or completing, while κόλασις here is the punishment accruing to the ungodly agents.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἄνευ γὰρ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ βουλῆς οὐδὲ στρουθὸς ἐν παγίδι ἐνπεσεῖν ἔχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: without God’s counsel not even a sparrow can fall into a trap
lexical_decisions.rationale: βουλή is “counsel” or “purpose,” and the ἔχει plus infinitive construction is represented idiomatically by “can.” The explicitly named trap is retained.

previous_passages.text: ‘See, Simon, what kind of God you wish to persuade us to be ungrateful toward! The earth still carries you, perhaps wishing to see who would dare to think as you do. For you were the first to dare what no one had dared, the first to utter what we heard for the first time. We were the first and only ones to witness God's boundless patience in the face of such impiety from you—not that of some other god, but of the one who created the world, against whom you dared to be impious. No chasms opened in the earth, no fire was sent down from heaven or advanced to burn people, no rain was withheld, no multitude of wild beasts was sent from the thickets, and God's destructive wrath did not begin even against us because of one sinner, as in the case of spiritual adultery, which is worse than adultery according to the flesh. For is not the one who then punished sins the God who created heaven and earth? For even now, most grievously blasphemed, he would have inflicted the greatest punishment. But, on the contrary, he is patient and calls us to reorientation toward God. He has destructive arrows stored in his treasuries for the destruction of the impious, which he will release like living creatures when he takes his seat to repay his enemies with judgment. Therefore let us fear the righteous God whose form the human body bears as an honor.’

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἴσως δὲ ἰδεῖν βουλομένῃ τίς σοι τὰ ὅμοια φρονεῖν τολμήσοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: perhaps wishing to see who would dare to think as you do
lexical_decisions.rationale: The feminine participle is read as continuing the personified earth, despite its oblique inflection beside the nominative earth. Perhaps qualifies the conjecture; the English does not replace the earth with an unexpressed masculine observer.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ὁ τότε ἐπεξελθὼν τὰ ἁμαρτήματα οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς κτίστης θεός;
lexical_decisions.chosen: For is not the one who then punished sins the God who created heaven and earth?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The printed negative question is retained rather than turned into a categorical identification or categorical denial. Its relation to the following counterfactual punishment and contrasting patience is rhetorically difficult. A reading that challenges the attribution of the earlier punishments to the creator is materially possible; the main text preserves the question rather than deleting the negative or resolving the theology by emendation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: calls us to reorientation toward God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied English policy uses reorientation for moral-spiritual redirection, with toward God where the context supports the destination. Here the creator's invitation contrasts with the preceding impiety against him; us is the contextually inferred addressee, not a claim that God himself must reorient.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: συντελοῦντα βέλη πρὸς συντέλειαν τῶν ἀσεβῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: destructive arrows ... for the destruction of the impious
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated completion or ending root describes final, destructive force. The English retains the destructive aim and the arrows image without supplying a specific weapon technology.

lexical_decisions.chosen: like living creatures
lexical_decisions.rationale: The life-bearing comparison is explicit; it does not say that the arrows are literally a named species of animal or angel.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς ἐπὶ μοιχείας πνευματικῆς τῆς κατὰ σάρκα χείρονος ὑπαρχούσης
lexical_decisions.chosen: as in the case of spiritual adultery, which is worse than adultery according to the flesh
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main reading takes adultery according to the flesh as the genitive of comparison and attaches worse being to spiritual adultery. It is favored by the surrounding rebuke, which presents Simon's impiety as especially serious. A material alternative takes adultery according to the flesh as subject of a genitive absolute: adultery according to the flesh being worse. That reverses the comparison and is not excluded by morphology alone. This is a disclosed attachment ambiguity, not an unverified printing defect.

revision_evidence.reason: Maintainer-approved October13 contextual repentance policy supersedes October11 reorientation default; actual new source review is required for every audited main-text hit, including explicit contextual exceptions
